artifacts.summary: Root-causes all six cited plan-to-file_scope divergences: #417 is a plan-authoring grammar deviation (confirmed by re-running the harvester against the real archived plan), #413's three citations and four of #417's eight paths are genuinely incomplete declarations deferred to completed task 430, and #424 is a since-fixed predicate bug that also exposed a still-live .claude/** containment loophole. Gives explicit PART A/B rulings, recommendations, and a defense-in-depth test plan.

memory_candidates.content: plan-file-scope-harvest.sh's 'one Files-to-modify path per backtick-dash line; a continuation line belongs to the preceding entry' grammar is not a parsing limitation -- it is the literal, intentionally mirrored contract documented in context/formats/plan-format.md. Before proposing to widen this grammar (e.g. to scan every backtick token in a block), check whether the same block legitimately contains non-path backtick tokens in descriptive prose (quoted headings, bare basenames) -- widening indiscriminately trades a silent-drop failure for a silent-garbage file_scope entry, which is worse because it can falsely legitimize an unrelated future edit under the Containment predicate.

context/formats/plan-format.md reserves a __WHOLE_TREE__ sentinel for a plan phase that invokes whole-tree regeneration (deploy-headless.sh / extension-picker reload), deliberately slashless so it is structurally inert against both the Overlap and Containment file_scope predicates. A plan phase that instead names .claude/** directly in its Files-to-modify block gets that literal path harvested into file_scope, and -- after git-commit-phase.sh's 2026-11-04 trailing-slash normalization fix (commit 2a945dca3) -- a bare '.claude/' file_scope entry now matches (contains) every .claude/** path, which is the opposite of the deploy-boundary rule's intent. Neither plan-file-scope-harvest.sh nor validate-artifact.sh currently refuses a harvested .claude/** path.

Technique for root-causing a historical scope-excursion/containment issue.jsonl entry: cross-reference the issue's ISO8601 timestamp against `git log --all --format="%H %ad %s" --date=iso -- specs/state.json` (and the relevant script's own git log) to place the drop event precisely relative to (a) when file_scope was last written for that task and (b) when any later bugfix to the containment predicate landed. This distinguished a genuine plan-authoring/harvester gap from a since-fixed implementation bug in task 446's research, where a naive reading of the issue text alone would have misattributed the cause.
